chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who forgets the Qunut in the Witr prayer or in other than the Witr prayer, he said: 'There is nothing upon him.' And he said: 'If he remembers it while he is bowing towards Ruku' before placing his hands on his knees, let him return standing and perform Qunut, then bow. And if he places his hands on his knees, let him proceed in his prayer and there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.يَضَعَ يَدَيْهِ عَلَى الرُّكْبَتَيْنِ: Placing hands on the knees (a key marker for the point of no return in this ruling)

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they forget the Qunut during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *Qunut* in Witr and other prayers, establishing a precise physical threshold for validity: the placement of hands on the knees marks the point of no return for this specific act of worship. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the distinction between obligatory (*fard*) and recommended (*mustahabb*) acts, ensuring that forgetfulness does not invalidate the prayer's structure while preserving the spiritual benefit of the supplication when remembered in time.
